windows-search.name: local_windows_search
windows-search.title: Search the Windows index
windows-search.description: Search indexed local files using native Windows Advanced Query Syntax (AQS), for example 'kind:document budget' or 'ext:pdf invoice'. Searches indexed filenames, properties, and content when a content filter is installed. English AQS keywords are supported. Only indexed locations are searched; an empty result does not prove a file does not exist. Returns absolute local paths that local_files_read can read if the Files plugin is enabled. Does not crawl folders or download files.

query.description: Native Windows AQS query, not SQL.

folder.description: Optional absolute local folder path. Restricts matches to this folder and its descendants.

limit.description: Maximum results; defaults to 20, capped at 100.

windows-clipboard.name: local_clipboard_get
windows-clipboard.title: Read clipboard text
windows-clipboard.description: Read the current Windows clipboard as plain text, locally. Returns hasText and text; empty/non-text clipboards return hasText=false. Text is limited to 50,000 characters with truncated=true when shortened. Does not read images, files, clipboard history, or monitor changes. Clipboard contents may be sensitive and returned text enters the normal chat/tool-result flow. Uses the existing execute-then-review flow, not a pre-access permission prompt.

windows-clipboard.name: local_clipboard_set
windows-clipboard.title: Copy text to the clipboard
windows-clipboard.description: Replace the current Windows clipboard contents with plain text (up to 50,000 characters). An empty string copies empty text. Existing clipboard formats/content are replaced; this cannot be undone by this tool. Does not read clipboard history or start monitoring. Requests no cloud/history storage for the copied data. Uses the existing execute-then-review flow, not a pre-access permission prompt.

windows-window-inspector.name: local_windows_get_active_window
windows-window-inspector.title: Get the active window
windows-window-inspector.description: Read metadata for the current foreground Windows window, which may be AIHappey itself. Returns window handle, process ID/name, title, class name and minimized state, or window=null if none is available. Does not switch focus, capture the screen or inspect UI controls. Metadata is live and may change. Uses the existing execute-then-review flow.

windows-window-inspector.name: local_windows_list_windows
windows-window-inspector.title: List open windows
windows-window-inspector.description: List visible, non-cloaked top-level Windows windows, including minimized windows, with handles, process IDs/names, titles and class names. Not an inventory of every running/background process or windows on other desktops. Results are bounded and may change. Use a returned windowHandle and processId with local_windows_inspect_window. No focusing, screen capture or UI actions. Uses the existing execute-then-review flow.

windows-window-inspector.name: local_windows_inspect_window
windows-window-inspector.title: Inspect window controls
windows-window-inspector.description: Read a bounded Windows UI Automation control-view tree for one visible top-level window returned by the window tools. Supply both its windowHandle and processId to detect stale/reused handles. Returns flat nodes with parent IDs, depth, control type, name, automation ID, class, enabled/offscreen status and available plain-text edit values. Password/protected nodes are redacted and not traversed. Never clicks, invokes, types, focuses, expands, captures screens, or elevates. Inaccessible/elevated apps, custom controls and hung providers may yield partial results or a safe error. Depth, nodes, text and waiting time are capped. Sensitive visible text may enter the normal chat/tool-result flow. Uses the existing execute-then-review flow, not a pre-access permission prompt.

windowHandle.description: Opaque hexadecimal windowHandle returned by a window tool; never a JSON number.

windows-ocr.name: local_ocr_list_languages
windows-ocr.title: List local OCR languages
windows-ocr.description: List installed Windows OCR recognition languages and the maximum supported image dimension. Runs locally and installs/downloads nothing. An empty list means the user needs to install a Windows OCR language pack through Windows Settings.

windows-ocr.name: local_ocr_recognize_text
windows-ocr.title: Recognize text in a local image
windows-ocr.description: Extract text from a local PNG, JPEG, BMP or TIFF image with installed Windows OCR, without any model/API/network request. Supply an absolute local path, optionally an installed BCP-47 language tag from local_ocr_list_languages; otherwise Windows user languages are used. Reads only the first image frame. Rejects network/device paths, links, oversized files and images above 16 megapixels or the native OCR dimension limit; does not resize. Returns text and bounded lines/word rectangles in decoded-image pixels, with truncation indicators. Maximum file size 20 MiB, text 50,000 characters, lines 500, words 2,000. No screen capture, PDF processing, language downloads, or external OCR fallback. Extracted text enters the normal chat/tool-result flow.

path.description: Absolute local image path; for example C:\Users\Alice\Pictures\error.png.

language.description: Optional installed Windows OCR language tag, such as en-US or nl-NL.

local-files.name: local_files_list
local-files.title: List shared files and folders
local-files.description: List references explicitly shared through the Windows Files page, including AI-created files. References contain stable IDs, paths, kind, and availability; the app does not copy file contents. Use IDs with the shared directory/read/create tools. Names may not be unique. Sharing a folder includes its descendants and permits creation of new files there. This list does not restrict the separate local_files_read absolute-path reader. Use nextCursor to continue; roots may change between calls.

cursor.description: Omit or use an empty string for the first page. For continuation, pass nextCursor returned by the previous shared-item listing unchanged.

local-files.name: local_files_list_directory
local-files.title: Browse a shared folder
local-files.description: List direct children of a shared folder or any nested subfolder. Pass the folder reference ID and a root-relative relativePath (omit for the root). Returned relativePath values are always relative to that shared root; use them to browse deeper or read files. No recursion or whole-disk scanning is performed. Returns files, folders, and explicit unsupported/denied/unavailable entries; links/junctions are never traversed. Pages are bounded; continue with nextCursor, the same ID and relativePath. Cursors are opaque, single-use, and valid only for this chat turn; restart the listing if expired. Directory contents can change between pages.

id.description: Shared folder ID returned by local_files_list.

relativePath.description: Subfolder path relative to the shared root; omitted or empty for the root. No absolute paths or dot/dot-dot segments.

cursor.description: Omit or use an empty string for the first page. For continuation, pass the single-use nextCursor returned by the previous directory page unchanged.

local-files.name: local_files_read_shared
local-files.title: Read a shared file
local-files.description: Read extracted text from an explicitly shared file ID, or from a file within a shared folder ID using a root-relative relativePath. Uses the same PDF/plain-text extractor as local_files_read; does not support OCR, Office formats, network paths or links. Paging is 1-based extracted-text lines, not PDF pages. Use nextLine as startLine to continue. Files can change between reads. A removed reference cannot be used, although another overlapping share may still allow access.

id.description: Shared file or folder reference ID.

relativePath.description: Required for a file inside a shared folder; omitted for a directly shared file.

local-files.name: local_files_create
local-files.title: Create a file in a shared folder
local-files.description: Create a NEW file inside an explicitly shared folder or existing nested subfolder. Requires the shared folder ID and a root-relative destination relativePath. Existing files/directories are never overwritten, renamed or deleted; missing parent folders are not created. No absolute paths, traversal, network paths or links. data is UTF-8 text by default; use encoding=base64 for explicitly encoded binary bytes. Maximum decoded file size is 1 MiB. Merely giving text a PDF/Office extension does not generate that format. The file is written to the real shared folder and registered as a reference on the Files page, not copied into app storage or executed. Sharing a folder authorizes creation; the existing execute-then-review flow is retained. A successful creation can include a warning if reference registration/refresh fails; do not retry creation of that same destination.

relativePath.description: New filename including any existing subfolders, relative to the shared root.

data.description: UTF-8 text or base64-encoded bytes, matching encoding.

local-files.name: local_files_read
local-files.title: Read a local file
local-files.description: Read text from an absolute local file path, including paths returned by local_windows_search. Uses the shared document extractor for PDFs and recognized text/Markdown/JSON/YAML/XML/source files. Does not support OCR, Office documents, downloads, network paths, device paths, or symbolic links. Paging uses 1-based line numbers in extracted text (not PDF page numbers). Results include totalLines, startLine, endLine, truncated, and nextLine; request nextLine as startLine to continue. A text-size ceiling can shorten a page at a complete line boundary. Files may change between calls.

path.description: Absolute local filesystem path, for example C:\Users\Alice\Documents\report.pdf.

maxLines.description: Maximum lines to return; defaults to 200, capped at 2000.
